# Computational Engine Principles {.unnumbered}

Part I establishes the foundation model as the primary computational engine of an agentic system. Moving beyond stateless single-token generation, we analyze the autoregressive execution cycle under physical hardware rooflines, non-deterministic execution contracts, grammar-constrained logit masks, and test-time deliberation algorithms that scale inference compute over complex reasoning topologies.

::: {#pri-vol3-trajectory-encapsulation .callout-principle title="Trajectory-level encapsulation"}

**Invariant**: The atomic unit of execution, resource allocation, and safety enforcement is not the token or the request, but the multi-step trajectory bounded by an invariant-enforcing runtime.

**Implication**: Serving runtimes must track budgets, cache allocations, and capability leases across the entire multi-turn trajectory rather than treating turns as isolated stateless requests.

:::

::: {#pri-vol3-memory-bandwidth-decoding .callout-principle title="Memory-bandwidth-bounded decoding"}

**Invariant**: Autoregressive token generation is fundamentally memory-bandwidth bound ($\mathcal{O}(1)$ arithmetic intensity during decode), making per-step latency a function of memory bus saturation rather than raw FLOP/s.

**Implication**: Computational engine efficiency requires architectural optimizations that maximize token reuse and operational intensity, including speculative verification and grammar-level logit masking.

:::

::: {#pri-vol3-test-time-scaling .callout-principle title="Test-time compute scaling and verification tax"}

**Invariant**: Allocating compute at inference time through deliberate search over reasoning paths can overcome base model parameter scaling limits, bounded by the Verification Tax ($C_{\text{ver}}$).

**Implication**: The agent runtime must dynamically allocate search breadth and depth against process reward verifiers to navigate the Pareto frontier of accuracy versus inference latency.

:::
